items.q: The listed causes of thrombotic microangiopathy are HUS, HELLP syndrome, malignant hypertension and the rheumatological conditions:
opts: Catastrophic APS and systemic lupus erythematosus
items.exp: Causes: HUS; HELLP; rheumatological condition – catastrophic APS, diffuse scleroderma; malignant hypertension. (Book p753)

items.q: The expansion of HELLP syndrome as written is:
opts: Hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme, low platelet
Hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme, low plasma volume
items.exp: HELLP syndrome (hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme, low platelet). (Book p753)

items.q: Match each condition with its renal-vessel category — 1) Catastrophic APS / diffuse scleroderma 2) Takayasu arteritis / polyarteritis nodosa 3) Malignant hypertension … A) Accelerated HTN + papilloedema B) Smaller vessels of kidney C) Larger vessels of kidney
items.exp: Catastrophic APS/diffuse scleroderma involve smaller vessels of kidney v/s larger vessels (Takayasu, PAN); malignant HTN = accelerated HTN + papilloedema. (Book p753)

items.q: Emergency hypertension in the malignant-HTN note is end-organ damage with a BP of at least:
items.exp: Emergency HTN: end organ damage + ≥180/120; new onset fundal changes: hemorrhage/exudate. (Book p753)
